explanation: Kiwi hunt at night, probing the soil with their beaks and finding food largely by smell, unusual for a bird. Sensitive pits near the tip may also feel prey moving.

claims.text: Kiwi have nostrils at the tip of the beak and use smell to find food such as worms.
The kākāpō, takahē and weka do not have nostrils at the tip of the beak.
Kiwi are mostly nocturnal and probe the soil with their beaks for food.
Kiwi have a cluster of sensory pits at the tip of the bill that may detect the movement of prey.

evidence.restatement: Kiwi are the only birds with nostrils at the tip of the bill, and they find worms and other prey by smell.
The kākāpō, takahē and weka have their nostrils at the base of the bill, like other birds.
Kiwi are mostly nocturnal and probe the soil with their bills for food.
